newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL adds partners to planned U.S. pipeline.
newsitem.headline: IPL adds partners to planned U.S. pipeline.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc added more corporate muscle to a proposed natural gas pipeline in the United States by announcing three new partners for its C$650 million Vector project.
Under the deal, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd will take a 35 percent interest in the pipeline and MCN Energy Group Inc will assume a 17.5 percent stake, IPL said.

Also, through a swap of equity interests, Columbia Gas System Inc would take an interest in Vector while IPL took a similar interest in the proposed Millennium pipeline project. The equity amounts had yet to be finalized.
The Vector line, announced in June, would ship one billion cubic feet of gas a day 344 miles to the Dawn hub in southern Ontario from Chicago.
From Dawn, existing and proposed pipeline connections would allow the movement of gas to markets in Ontario and the U.S. Northeast.
Dawn is also near the origin of the 650 million cubic feet a day Millennium pipeline, proposed by Columbia, Westcoast Energy Inc, CMS Energy Corp and MCN.
That pipeline would extend 380 miles to Westchester County, New York from a connection at Lake Erie.
IPL Chief Executive Brian MacNeill said in a statement that the move furthered the company's goal to link up with major energy players to develop low-cost gas transport for western Canadian supply.
The company also has a stake in the proposed C$3.6 billion Alliance Pipeline, which would ship Canadian gas to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.

The producer-backed Alliance project last week won preliminary approval from the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, a development seen as a big step toward the 1.3 billion cubic feet a day line's go-ahead. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
